item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 121722
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Sat Sep 12 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Norbert, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of
the Baja California Peninsula.

Central and Western East Pacific (EP97):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with an area of low pressure
located several hundred miles southwest of the southwestern coast
of Mexico have become a little less organized this morning.
Environmental conditions appear conducive for development, however,
and a tropical depression is expected to form during the next couple
of days while it moves generally west-northwestward to westward over
the central and western portions of the eastern Pacific basin. For
more information, including gale warnings, please see the High Seas
Forecast issued by the National Weather Service.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...80 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Well Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
A broad area of low pressure located several hundred miles
southeast of Hilo, Hawaii, is producing disorganized showers and
thunderstorms. Development of this system, if any, is expected to
be slow to occur while it drifts generally west-northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...10 percent.

&&

High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service
can be found under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN02
KWBC, and on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

$$
Forecaster Roberts

item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Sat Sep 12 2026 
000
WTPZ34 KNHC 122057
TCPEP4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Norbert Advisory Number  13
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
1100 AM HST Sat Sep 12 2026
 
...NORBERT A LITTLE WEAKER...
...NOW EXPECTED TO DISSIPATE EAST-SOUTHEAST OF HAWAII BY THE MIDDLE
OF NEXT WEEK...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 AM HST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.6N 129.6W
ABOUT 1325 MI...2135 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
ABOUT 1675 MI...2690 KM E OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1000 MB...29.53 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM HST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Norbert was
located near latitude 17.6 North, longitude 129.6 West. Norbert is
moving toward the west-northwest near 12 mph (19 km/h). A 
west-northwestward to westward motion is expected during the next 
several days.
 
Satellite-derived wind data indicate that maximum sustained winds 
have decreased to near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher gusts. Little 
change in strength is expected over the next 24 hours, but 
weakening is likely to begin on Sunday. Norbert could degenerate 
into a remnant low by Wednesday and dissipate by Thursday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105 miles (165 km)
mainly to the north of the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1000 mb (29.53 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Berg

item.title: Tropical Storm Norbert Forecast Discussion Number 13
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Sat Sep 12 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 122057
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Norbert Discussion Number  13
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
1100 AM HST Sat Sep 12 2026
 
A 1712 UTC ASCAT-B pass revealed that Norbert's center is located 
near the southern edge of a compact mass of deep convection, and the 
wind field is asymmetric, favoring the northern side. The 
scatterometer data showed peak wind vectors of 42 kt within the 
northwestern quadrant, and based on that data, the current 
intensity is lowered to 45 k.

Norbert continues to move west-northwestward, or 285/10 kt, located 
to the south of the subtropical ridge extending westward from 
northern Mexico. The ridge is expected to keep Norbert on a 
west-northwestward to westward heading for the remainder of the 
forecast period. However, there has been another northward shift in 
the track model guidance, and the NHC official forecast has been 
moved in that direction using a blend of the previous forecast with 
the latest HCCA and GDMI aids, which lie along the northern 
boundary of the guidance envelope.

The additional northward shift in Norbert's expected track will 
take it further into the zone of strong westerly shear that extends 
across much of the central Pacific basin, including over Hawaii. 
Little change in strength is expected during the next 24 hours 
while the shear still remains relatively low, but increasing shear 
and a marginal thermodynamic environment should cause additional 
weakening to begin on Sunday. In fact, the nearly all of the models 
respond to the hostile environment by showing Norbert dissipating 
into a trough of low pressure several hundred miles east-southeast 
of Hawaii potentially as early as Wednesday. For this update, the 
NHC forecast shows Norbert degenerating into a remnant low by 
Wednesday and dissipating by Thursday before reaching the longitude 
of the Hawaiian Islands.
